name: ARES defensive-swarm scaling policy
statusNote: Auto-scaling stays OFF in Phase 1. This file states the policy only — no scaling code runs, no instances are spawned, and nothing in this file can enable scaling on its own. Enabling it is a Phase 3 decision, by Merlin's explicit word.

incident.description: An active, corroborated attack campaign justifies temporary dedicated cohort-tracking capacity.

load.description: Sustained request rate exceeds what current instances score within latency budget (p99 scoring latency above threshold for N minutes).

surface.description: A new route, service, or deployment widens the attack surface and the policy maps it to dedicated coverage.

caps.capBreach: Breaching the cost cap pages Merlin and freezes further scaling until he raises it.
caps.scaleDown: Instances retire automatically when load drops; idle instances never linger to accumulate cost or attack surface.

killSwitch.control: Dashboard toggle in the ARES console (Defense modules) or ARES_PHASE1_KILL_SWITCH=1 in env.
killSwitch.description: One flag, two effects, immediate: all auto-scaling freezes (already off) and all Phase 1 non-determinism — rotating thresholds, watch-band randomization, jitter — switches off, with scoring falling back to the static v0 heuristics.
killSwitch.state: Read live from the console; this file states the rule, not the current state.

audit.description: Each spawn, retire, cap-hit, and kill-switch activation writes an immutable record to ares_audit_log (timestamp, trigger, policy version, instance id, resources granted, cost accrued, Hub's stated reason).
audit.table: ares_audit_log (schema addition, unexecuted until Merlin runs supabase-additions.sql)

decisionRule: Replication is never triggered by the field agents themselves — only the Hub decides, against this versioned policy file Merlin can read.
